description: The branching game's words: a story told in turns. Each NODE is one situation and one reported decision; each of its choices moves the meter and names what happens next (another node, or an ending). A node's id is a data-question-id row on the page, and its outcome codes are that row's data-measures, never in here. A node the learner's path never reaches is reported as no decision (none, wrong) when the debrief opens, so it counts against them: put EVERY node on the all-right walk (the choice marked correct at each node leads on through all of them), let wrong choices skip ahead, end the story or lower the meter until a node's `leave` turns it -- the game warns in the console when the right walk misses a node, because a flawless learner would then be scored below full marks. Ask the person for every rule and source you were not given.

title.description: The story's title, on its first screen and its debrief.

meter.description: What is at stake, shown as a meter from 0 to 100 that starts at 50. A right choice raises it by 10, a hesitant one lowers it by 10 and a wrong one by 25, so two wrong acts in a row empty it; while a turn's clock has run out it drains; under 35 (its «منخفض» band) a node with `leave` is never entered; at 0 the story ends early.

label.description: The meter's name, one or two words: «ثقة العميل», «سلامة الفريق», «الوقت».

start.description: The id of the node the story opens on.

nodes.description: The situations, in the order the debrief and the feedback sheet list them (not the order a learner meets them, which the choices decide). Every node must be reachable from start, and every path must reach an ending.

id.description: The interaction id the LMS receives: ASCII, unique in the lecture, never the id of an ending, and the data-question-id of one row on the page. Take it from the client's alignment document; never invent it.

title.description: Two to four words naming the moment («الاستقبال», «الفحص»): on the trail of steps taken, and as the debrief's row.

speaker.description: Optional: who speaks or acts in this node («العميل»), shown under the character's picture.

text.description: The situation, one to three short sentences the learner reads while the clock runs.

leave.description: Optional: the id of an ending the story goes to INSTEAD of this node when the learner arrives with the meter under 35 -- the stake changing what happens next («لم يعد يثق بكم فخرج»). The ending screen says the meter did it; the nodes never met are reported none/wrong. Give it to a node late on the spine, never to start.

rule.description: What to do here and why, in one sentence: shown after the consequence of any choice, and in the debrief.

source.description: The citation the learner reads under the rule («المصدر: …»). Ask the person; never invent it. Left empty, the release lists it as left for the person.

choices.description: What the learner may do, two to four. The game shuffles their order on screen, seeded by the ids, so the right one is not always first.

id.description: The response the LMS receives (a, b, c): ASCII, unique inside its node. The label never travels on the wire.

label.description: What the learner does, in the first person, five to ten words; never a verdict that tells the answer.

result.description: correct raises the meter by 10, neutral (a hesitant act) lowers it by 10, wrong lowers it by 25.

consequence.description: What happens because of this choice, told as the story's next beat, before the rule: name the behaviour, never the learner.

next.description: The id of the node or the ending this choice leads to.

endings.description: Where the story can end, each reached by some choice's next. Endings are not decisions and report nothing; the meter running out is an ending of the game's own.

id.description: ASCII, and never the id of a node.

title.description: The ending's name, two to four words.

text.description: What came of the path, one or two sentences.

tone.description: good: the path the rules lead to; mixed: part of it; bad: a path that went wrong.

slots.description: Optional: the art hand's own pictures for the game's two picture slots (game.json names their sizes). Each value is a path under the lecture's assets, such as "../assets/customer.png"; a slot left out keeps the game's own placeholder.

character.description: The person the learner deals with, from the waist up; transparent around them.

scene.description: Where the story happens, behind everything; opaque, 1280x720.
